name: lake maidens

attributes.attribute: lived in palaces beneath the lake waves
captured by stealing a robe or comb
vanished when her taboo was broken

sources: Rhys, John. Celtic Folklore: Welsh and Manx. Oxford: Clarendon Press, 1941.
Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Lake maidens were folkloric characters across the Celtic lands. Lakes were seen as entrances to the Otherworld, and fairy women lived in palaces beneath the waves. These maidens were hard to capture as wives for human men. A man had to steal something from the maiden, such as her robe of feathers from a swan or her comb. Then she came to shore and became an industrious and pleasant wife. Yet each maiden placed a taboo on her husband's conduct. One man could not show surprise at his son. Another could not see his wife on Sundays. The Welsh maiden Nelferch allowed only three mistakes. When a lake maiden's rule was broken, she vanished and went back to her watery home.

okr.objective: Present lake maidens as fairy women who lived beneath the lakes and could be captured as wives.
key_results: Describe how a man captured a lake maiden by theft.
List the taboos placed on husbands, including Nelferch's three mistakes.
State that a broken rule made the maiden vanish.
